newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells electricity to Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells electricity to Yugoslavia.

text.p: Bulgaria's debt-ridden National Electricity Company (NEC) has started exporting electricity to rump Yugoslavia due to a sharp rise in its consumption, NEC executive director Vassil Anastasov said on Thursday.
He said the NEC started electricity exports to Belgrade a week ago. He declined to give details.
"We will export electricity depending on their needs and the quantities will be different each day," Anastasov told Reuters.
He said the exports would not affect Bulgaria's own electricity supplies.
An NEC official who declined to be named said the company hoped to earn $1.5 million from its exports to Yugoslavia.
The NEC is one of 70 indebted state companies due to be isolated from credits while they are restructured under a government austerity programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
Bulgaria's central bank has barred local banks from lending to the NEC but the company can draw loans from foreign banks.
NEC officials said the company, which produces 87 percent of Bulgaria's power, would make ends meet during the coming winter without having to seek loans.
The company plans to sign on Thursday a loan agreement for four million dollars with ING Bank, part of Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV.

"If we also receive the promised 11 million Ecus from the EU's Phare programme to buy coal for the thermal power plant in Varna, I am almost certain that we will manage with our own funds," said the NEC's Krassimir Kanev.
Bulgaria, currently in the throes of an economic crisis, imports some 80 percent of its energy resources.
